controls.rule: Every contributing or moderating mutation refuses the request unless a user is logged in.
A user may only act on behalf of an organization of which they are a member (and must name one if they belong to several).
A conflict-of-interest statement counts as valid only for one year after it was filed; expired statements fail every COI check.
Accepted evidence items and assertions (Moderated records) cannot be destroyed; the destroy is aborted.
A new or revised evidence item is refused if an identical non-rejected evidence item already exists.
Evidence items cannot be submitted against a non-existent or deprecated molecular profile.
An evidence item whose source is marked retracted by Retraction Watch fails validation.
An evidence item whose source is deprecated fails validation.
Evidence type, significance, direction, disease and therapy fields must be mutually consistent (and disease/therapies not deprecated) or validation fails.
A newly submitted evidence item needs a description of at least 50 characters.
The optional submission comment, if given, must be at least 10 characters.
On submission the evidence item gets a review due date: 14 days for Predictive evidence, 30 days otherwise.
Only signed-in editors may pull items from the moderation queue endpoint.
Pulling from the moderation queue requires a current conflict-of-interest statement.
The moderation queue orders submitted evidence flagged items first, then by earliest review due date, then oldest submission.
The next-item endpoint never hands an editor an evidence item they submitted themselves.
The next-item endpoint only hands out items that are unassigned or assigned to the requesting editor.
The GraphQL review_queue option lists only submitted, unflagged evidence not submitted by the requester, ordered by review due date then id.
A daily job reassigns submitted evidence past its review due date to another editor, resets the due date to 7 days and increments the escalation count.
The review assigner never picks the evidence item's submitter (or excluded editors) as reviewer.
The review assigner only considers editors/admins with a valid conflict-of-interest statement.
The review assigner skips editors who already hold 25 open (submitted) assignments, choosing the least-loaded remaining editor.
Moderating an evidence item to the status it already has is refused.
A comment is required when rejecting or reverting an evidence item.
No comment may be supplied when accepting an evidence item.
An evidence item cannot be accepted while its source is retracted or deprecated.
The submitter of an evidence item may reject it themselves without being an editor.
Policy: editors with a valid COI statement may accept evidence they did not submit.
Admins may accept their own submitted evidence once it has waited in the queue more than 180 days.
Users may not accept their own submitted evidence (unless the admin stale-submission exception applies).
Any other moderation of an evidence item (accept, reject, revert) requires editor role or higher.
Rejecting an evidence item supersedes all of its open revisions.
Rejecting an evidence item moves active organization approvals of its linked assertions to requires_review.
Withdrawal is permitted only to the signed-in submitter while the item is still submitted, not linked to any assertion and not flagged.
An evidence item that already has accepted revisions cannot be withdrawn and must be rejected by an editor.
Evidence items cited by a submitted/revised assertion must exist and be in a valid state.
An assertion needs at least one evidence item unless its type is Oncogenic.
Assertion type, significance, direction, disease, therapy, codes, AMP level and NCCN fields must be mutually consistent or validation fails.
The optional assertion submission comment, if given, must be at least 10 characters.
Moderating an assertion to the status it already has is refused.
A comment is required when rejecting or reverting an assertion.
No comment may be supplied when accepting an assertion.
The submitter of an assertion may reject it themselves without being an editor.
Users may not accept their own submitted assertions.
Moderating an assertion otherwise requires editor role or higher.
Reverting an accepted assertion that has active organization approvals back to submitted requires the reopen privilege.
Admins, and editors with a valid COI and an explicit reopen_privilege, may send decided items back to the queue.
An assertion cannot be accepted while any of its supporting evidence items is not accepted.
Rejecting an assertion moves its active organization approvals to requires_review.
Changing the AMP level or significance of an accepted assertion moves its active approvals to requires_review.
Only accepted assertions can be approved on behalf of an organization.
A flagged assertion cannot be approved.
An organization cannot approve an assertion it already has an active approval for.
Approving or revoking approval requires the user to hold approval privileges for the organization.
Approving an assertion requires a valid conflict-of-interest statement.
Revoking an approval requires a reason comment of at least 10 characters.
Revocation requires exactly one active or requires_review approval from that organization.
Suggesting a revision requires an explanatory comment of at least 10 characters (same on all suggest*Revision mutations).
A rejected evidence item can no longer receive revision suggestions.
The revised object must pass model validation before revisions are created.
A revision suggestion must change at least one field.
A suggestion is refused if every proposed revision duplicates an existing open revision (duplicates are reused, not recreated).
Only revisions in status 'new' can be accepted.
Revisions accepted (or rejected) together must all concern the same subject.
Revisions accepted together may not target the same field.
An optional acceptance comment, if given, must be at least 10 characters.
The submitter of a still-submitted evidence item or assertion may accept revisions to it without editor role or COI checks.
Accepting revisions otherwise requires editor role.
Accepting revisions requires a valid conflict-of-interest statement.
A user may not accept a revision they suggested.
Only revisions in status 'new' can be rejected.
Rejecting revisions requires a reason comment of at least 10 characters.
Any user may reject a revision they suggested themselves.
Rejecting someone else's revision requires editor role.
Rejecting someone else's revision requires a valid conflict-of-interest statement.
A revision already accepted or rejected cannot change status (model validation).
Accepting a revision supersedes all other open revisions on the same subject and field.
Accepting revisions to evidence level, significance, direction or molecular profile of an accepted evidence item returns it to submitted.
Accepting revisions to an assertion or to an evidence item linked to assertions moves active approvals to requires_review.
A monthly job supersedes open revisions older than one year that have had no comment in the last 90 days.
A comment body must be at least 10 characters.
A comment body may not exceed 20,000 characters.
Users may only delete their own comments.
An already deleted comment cannot be deleted again.
Raising a flag requires a description of at least 10 characters.
A user cannot open a second flag on an entity where they already have an open flag.
Raising a flag marks the flagged entity as flagged.
Flags on accepted assertions with an active organization approval get high priority.
Flagging an entity moves its active organization approvals to requires_review.
When an accepted flaggable has open flags from at least 3 distinct users it is returned to submitted status.
The nightly Retraction Watch job flags (as CIViCbot) every evidence item whose source is newly marked as retracted.
When a source is no longer retracted, the job resolves CIViCbot retraction flags on its evidence items.
When a source is no longer retracted, the job flags its rejected evidence items for re-evaluation.
A weekly job flags (as CIViCbot) variants that share an Allele Registry ID, unless such a bot flag is already open.
Only open flags can be resolved.
Resolving a flag requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
Admins may resolve any open flag.
Editors in the 'CIViC Editorial Team' organization may resolve flags raised by CIViCbot (no COI or own-submission check).
The user who raised a flag may resolve it.
The submitter of the flagged entity may not resolve flags raised against their own submission.
Resolving another user's flag requires editor role.
Resolving another user's flag requires a valid conflict-of-interest statement.
A resolved flag must record its resolving user (model validation).
When the last open flag on an entity is resolved, the entity's flagged marker is cleared.
Approvals pushed to requires_review by a flag return to active once the subject has no open flags left.
A source suggestion requires a justification comment of at least 10 characters.
The suggested source must exist, and any named molecular profile, disease or therapies must exist and not be deprecated.
A source suggestion must name a molecular profile or a disease.
A suggestion is refused if an open ('new') suggestion already exists for the same source, molecular profile and disease.
On creation a suggestion is assigned to the editor/admin (not the suggester) with the fewest assigned suggestions.
An editor changing a suggestion's status must have a valid conflict-of-interest statement.
A suggestion cannot be marked curated unless its source has a submitted or accepted evidence item.
Only transitions new->curated, new->rejected, curated->new and rejected->new are allowed.
Curated or rejected suggestions may be put back to 'new' (requeued).
A weekly job rejects suggestions that stayed 'new' with no update for more than two years, with an automatic reason.

notes: Uncertain or noteworthy observations: (1) EvidenceItem accept: EvidenceItemPolicy#accept? requires editor+valid COI, but when it returns false for a non-submitter the mutation falls through to the plain editor check (moderate_evidence_item.rb:66), so an editor without a valid COI can still accept evidence; K28 coded as P, COI not effectively enforced for EID moderation. ModerateAssertion has no COI check at all. (2) Reverting an accepted evidence item to submitted needs only editor role; the reopen privilege (K46/K47) is only checked for assertions with active approvals. (3) Moderation::Withdrawal (K34/K35) and EvidenceReviewAssigner#assign! are not called from any mutation/controller/job in this snapshot; only #pick is used by the escalation job, so no reviewer is assigned at submission and the K20-K22 rules apply only on escalation. Withdrawal looks like unwired code. (4) Selection inconsistency: the controller queue orders flagged items first (K15) while the GraphQL review_queue excludes flagged items (K18). (5) retraction_watch.rb:83 references an undefined variable `text` in resolve_eid_flags, so the automatic flag resolution (K92) would raise at runtime. (6) AcceptRevisions#auto_accept_trivial_followups is disabled (auto_accept_trivial? returns false), and the old 'resolve flag requeues accepted item' branch in Actions::ResolveFlag is behind `if false`; neither coded. Comment in Flag model about auto-closing year-old flags is a TODO only. (7) UpdateSourceSuggestionStatus: non-editor users (curators) can change status with no role check at all; only editors are COI-checked. Source-suggestion curator auto-assignment has no COI check. (8) AcceptRevisions P rule (K67) lets the submitter of a still-submitted EID/assertion accept revisions to it, including revisions they suggested themselves (own-revision check is skipped). (9) Actions::ResolveFlag uses `save` (not save!) so the K103 validation failure would be silent. (10) ApproveAssertion has no own-submission check. (11) Model field validators (K9, K38) and the 50-char description rule were coded once each although they contain many sub-rules. (12) Deprecation guards on variants/MPs/diseases/therapies/sources that block deprecation while open revisions or live evidence reference them (deprecate_variant.rb, deprecation_validator.rb) were treated as entity curation, not review controls, and not coded. (13) Several G entries in 'selection'/'allocation' (K16, K17, K20-K22) are filters, not refusals; mode G chosen as closest.
